statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail is elevated at the European cash open because technology-led futures weakness aligns with oil above $107 and near-5% Treasury yields; granular NQ retracement evidence remains unavailable.
recommendation: The orange mapping reflects multiple current amplifiers rather than a confirmed no-retracement path. Further escalation requires verified persistent one-way NQ structure; two-way rotations or meaningful gap repair would support de-escalation.
headline: European cash open tests the technology gap under oil and rates pressure
body: The latest verified snapshot showed Nasdaq futures down about 1.3% versus roughly 0.5% for S&P futures. Reuters then kept Brent above $107, yields near 5%, and AI-linked technology weakness active. No equally fresh granular NQ pullback sequence was verified at the cutoff.

lookbackSummary: Tail stayed low through Sunday, moved to WATCH at the Globex reopening, and entered the elevated band as technology weakness, energy shock and rate pressure aligned. Published assessments stayed orange from 23:00 UTC through 06:00 UTC.
outlookSummary: Europe is the immediate persistence checkpoint. Tail stays in the upper 20s if the technology discount resists retracement, eases with two-way trade, and rises again near the U.S. open only if failed pullbacks appear.

forecast.analysis: Europe opens with verified Nasdaq futures underperforming S&P futures while Brent exceeds $107 and the 10-year yield nears 5%. Granular NQ retracement evidence is still incomplete.
drivers: Europe cash open tests persistence of the technology discount
